module purpose: neorv32_gptmr accepts bus writes to a control register and a threshold register, selects one bit of clkgen_i as a timer tick, counts until the count equals the threshold, and latches an interrupt-pending flag. It returns control, threshold, count, and pending status on the bus response record, exports the enable state on clkgen_en_o, and drives irq_o from the pending flag.

use-case flows.value: control-register write that updates the timer enable bit, prescaler bits, and the interrupt-clear request
threshold value written into the held compare register
selected clkgen_i bit captured as a tick and used to clear, increment, or wrap the counter depending on enable and match
interrupt pending status set on a threshold match, cleared by clear request or disable, and driven on irq_o
control bits, pending status, threshold, and current count returned on bus_rsp_o.data according to the accessed word
active-low rstn_i clears control, threshold, clear request, tick, count, and pending state to known values

conceptual assets.concept: Timer enable configuration — whether the counter and interrupt logic are enabled
conceptual assets.reasoning: The enable bit is stored in ctrl by the clocked write at line 76, then used to drive clkgen_en_o at line 106, to force timer.count to zero when disabled at lines 118-119, and to qualify irq_pnd generation and clearing at lines 141-148. Integrity is established because these implemented behaviors become incorrect if the held enable value is corrupted; availability is also established because the value is held in ctrl and returned on reads at line 89, although the bus request/response ports are transport records and are not reported as structural assets.

conceptual assets.concept: Timer prescaler configuration — which clkgen_i source is selected as the timer tick
conceptual assets.reasoning: The prescaler bits are stored in ctrl by the clocked writes at lines 77-79 and are used as the selector in `clkgen_i(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl(ctrl_prsc2_c downto ctrl_prsc0_c))))` at line 117; the map records this as ctrl SELECTS timer.tick at occurrence 12. Integrity is established because a wrong held selection changes which input clock source advances the timer; availability is also established because the setting is held in ctrl and read back at lines 90-92, with the transport bus port excluded from structural reporting.

conceptual assets.concept: Timer threshold value — the held compare value that defines when the timer matches
conceptual assets.reasoning: The threshold register is written at line 84, returned on reads at line 96, and compared against the current count at line 131, where timer.thres CONSTRAINS timer.match. Integrity is established because corrupting this stored value changes both the implemented match point and the reported threshold; availability is also established because the value is held until rewritten or reset.

conceptual assets.concept: Timer count state — the current counter value maintained by the timer core
conceptual assets.reasoning: timer.count is cleared on reset at line 115, forced to zero when disabled at line 119, wrapped to zero on a match at line 122, incremented at line 124, compared to timer.thres at line 131, and returned on reads at line 98. Integrity is established because both the implemented match/interrupt behavior and the reported count become incorrect if this state is corrupted; availability is established conditionally by the RTL because the next count value is produced on rising edges when enabled and timer.tick is asserted, otherwise the state is reset or wrapped by the visible conditions at lines 118-124.

conceptual assets.concept: Threshold-match decision — whether the current count equals the threshold
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes `timer.match <= '1' when (timer.count = timer.thres) else '0';` at line 131; the map records timer.match CONSTRAINED_BY timer.count and timer.thres there. This decision is then used to wrap the counter at lines 121-124 and to set irq_pnd at line 142, so integrity is established because both flows depend on the correctness of the equality result; availability is also established because the comparator continuously produces the decision from the current stored operands.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt pending state — the latched report that a threshold match has occurred
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_pnd is set to '1' on a match at line 143, cleared by irq_clr at line 145, forced to '0' when disabled at line 148, returned on reads at line 94, and driven out on irq_o at line 154. Integrity is established because the module's interrupt reporting flow depends on this stored state matching those update rules; availability is also established because the state is retained between clock edges and delivered on irq_o until one of the RTL-visible clear conditions occurs.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt-clear request — the bus-written command that clears the pending interrupt
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_clr is reset low at line 65, forced low each cycle at line 71, captured from the control write at line 81, and used to clear irq_pnd at lines 144-145; the map records irq_clr GATES irq_pnd at occurrence 5. Integrity is established because a wrong stored clear request would incorrectly retain or clear the pending interrupt state; availability is established because the qualifying control write produces this one-cycle stored request in the clocked bus-access process.
